Gamma and beta functions

Source: R/gamma.R
gamma-functions.Rd

The gamma function and its relatives, evaluated with the same kernels as scipy.special, under SciPy's names and argument order. Functions marked "complex" take the complex path when given a complex argument and return complex; real input always stays real (sc_gamma(-1) is NaN).

Usage

sc_gamma(z)

sc_gammaln(x)

sc_loggamma(z)

sc_rgamma(z)

sc_gammasgn(x)

sc_psi(z)

sc_beta(a, b)

sc_betaln(a, b)

sc_binom(x, y)

sc_poch(z, m)

sc_gammainc(a, x)

sc_gammaincc(a, x)

sc_gammaincinv(a, y)

sc_gammainccinv(a, y)

sc_betainc(a, b, x)

sc_betaincc(a, b, x)

sc_betaincinv(a, b, y)

sc_betainccinv(a, b, y)

Arguments

z, x

Numeric vector; for z, also complex.

a, b, y, m

Numeric vectors; for the incomplete gamma functions a is the shape and y a probability.

Value

A double vector, or a complex vector for complex input.

Details

  • sc_gamma(): \(\Gamma(z)\), complex. Base R: gamma().

  • sc_gammaln(): \(\log|\Gamma(x)|\). Base R: lgamma().

  • sc_loggamma(): the principal branch of \(\log \Gamma(z)\), complex, with a branch cut on the negative real axis. For real z < 0 it is NaN, unlike sc_gammaln().

  • sc_rgamma(): \(1 / \Gamma(z)\), complex; zero at the poles.

  • sc_gammasgn(): the sign of \(\Gamma(x)\).

  • sc_psi(): the digamma function \(\psi(z)\), complex. Base R: digamma().

  • sc_beta(), sc_betaln(): \(B(a, b)\) and \(\log|B(a, b)|\). Base R: beta(), lbeta().

  • sc_betainc(), sc_betaincc(): the regularised incomplete beta function \(I_x(a, b)\) and its complement. Base R: pbeta(x, a, b) and pbeta(x, a, b, lower.tail = FALSE). At the limits a or b equal to 0 or Inf, SciPy's pointwise limits in x are returned.

  • sc_betaincinv(), sc_betainccinv(): their inverses in x. Base R: qbeta(y, a, b) and qbeta(y, a, b, lower.tail = FALSE).

The incomplete beta functions and their inverses are evaluated, as in SciPy, with Boost.Math (from the BH package) rather than xsf.

  • sc_binom(): the binomial coefficient for real x and y. Base R: choose().

  • sc_poch(): the Pochhammer symbol \(\Gamma(z + m) / \Gamma(z)\).

  • sc_gammainc(), sc_gammaincc(): the regularised lower and upper incomplete gamma functions \(P(a, x)\) and \(Q(a, x)\). Base R: pgamma(x, a) and pgamma(x, a, lower.tail = FALSE); note the argument order.

  • sc_gammaincinv(), sc_gammainccinv(): their inverses in x. Base R: qgamma(y, a) and qgamma(y, a, lower.tail = FALSE).

Arguments are recycled: each must have length one or the common length. NA gives NA; NaN is evaluated as SciPy does. The result takes its dimensions, or else its names, from the arguments as base R arithmetic does. Conditions the kernels raise, such as a pole, are handled as sc_seterr() says.

Windows

R on Windows is built with Rtools, whose C library (mingw-w64 v11) evaluates sin() and cos() inaccurately for arguments beyond about 1e5, as base R's own sin() shows there. Complex arguments with a part that large, and real ones where the kernel takes a sine of such a value, are correspondingly inaccurate on Windows only.

See also

https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/special.html#gamma-and-related-functions

Examples

sc_gamma(c(0.5, 5))
#> [1]  1.772454 24.000000
sc_gamma(1 + 1i)
#> [1] 0.4980157-0.1549498i
sc_loggamma(-2.5 + 0i)
#> [1] -0.05624372-9.424778i
sc_beta(2, 3)
#> [1] 0.08333333
sc_errstate(sc_gamma(-1), singular = "warn")
#> Warning: sc_gamma: singular in 1 element, first at index 1.
#> [1] NaN
